overexpression of the udk gene, encoding a uridine kinase, antagonizes the Gp2 function during T7 infection and consequently results in the accumulation of non-terminated T7 transcripts.
the overexpression of udc mimics the absence Gp2 function during T7 infection and therefore abrogates successful T7 infection.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the T 7 genome and with the role of the host-encoded udk gene in T7 phage infection.
the regulation of the T 7 genome during the infection of Escheri c ia coli.
the molecular mechanisms underlying T7 infection and with the role of Gp 2 in T7 transcriptional control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Gp2 is not a simple terminator, but rather an essential factor for the successful transcription of the T 7 genome.
the transcriptional control of the T7 phage genome is a very complex process that is influenced by a number of factors.
the T7 genome, like many other phage genomes, is regulated by a multitude of host- and phage-encoded factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T7 Gp 2 protein is a potent inhibitor for the E. coli RNA polymerase and the overexpression of E. coli uridine kinase (Udk) protein can antagonize the Gp2 activity.

The main takeaway from our work is that
T7 infection can be used as a model to investigate the role of host-encoded factors in the transcription of T7 genes.
